rendered:
Coprecipitation window: the NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated in a narrow pH range, between 10 and 12[1]. Why: simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is difficult because of the varying solubility product Ksp of their hydroxides. simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron,[2] is challenged by the bility product Ksp of the resulting hydroxide precipitates[3]. Aluminum hydroxide starts precipitating at a lower pH than nickel and iron hydroxides, which precipitate beyond pH 6[4]. This narrows the usable window to the range above, in which NFA precursors form successfully in hydroxide form.

From precursor to cathode powder: filtered, washed, and dried[5] to obtain the hydroxide precursors. These are mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.) and calcined in an O2-rich environment at >600 °C[6]. The resulting NFA cathode powder is then cast into electrodes by roll-to-roll slot-die coating and assembled into cobalt-free pouch cells.
